original_question: Are these two kerGV ’s trivial or not?
target_in_paper: Question 9.11 in §9.3.1 (Yoshihiko Mitsumatsu): whether the two Godbillon-Vey kernels attached to \(\pi_1(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty)\) and \(H_3(B\Gamma_H;\mathbb Z)\) are trivial. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target: it keeps the exact narrow focus on “the two kerGV’s” and asks the same yes/no question as Question 9.11, without drifting to neighboring problems such as determining \(H_2(B\Gamma_H;\mathbb Z)\), transverse loops in \(B\bar\Gamma_1^\omega\), or simplicity of \(\Gamma_H\). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: The draft does not say what the “two” kernels are: they are \(\ker(GV:\pi_1(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty)\to\mathbb R)\) and \(\ker(GV:H_3(B\Gamma_H;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb R)\). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

It omits the ambient objects: \(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty\) and \(B\bar\Gamma_1^\omega\) are the smooth and real-analytic codimension-one Haefliger classifying spaces considered in §9.3, and \(\Gamma_H\) is the discrete “Haefliger group” for which \(B\bar\Gamma_1^\omega\) is a \(K(\Gamma_H,1)\). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

It does not specify coefficients and target: the homology group is \(H_3(-;\mathbb Z)\), while the Godbillon-Vey map lands in \(\mathbb R\). ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

It leaves implicit the split nature of the problem: the preceding paragraph records \(\pi_1(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty)\cong \mathbb R\oplus \ker GV\) and \(H_3(B\Gamma_H;\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb R\oplus \ker GV\), coming from a surjective Godbillon-Vey map together with sections due to Tsuboi and Morita et al. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

It does not clarify that “trivial” means the zero subgroup/kernel, equivalently asking whether the relevant Godbillon-Vey homomorphism is already an isomorphism onto \(\mathbb R\) in each case. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: Let \(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty\) and \(B\bar\Gamma_1^\omega\) denote the smooth and real-analytic codimension-one Haefliger classifying spaces, and let \(\Gamma_H\) be the discrete Haefliger group with \(B\bar\Gamma_1^\omega\simeq K(\Gamma_H,1)\). The preceding discussion records two split Godbillon-Vey surjections, one on \(\pi_1(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty)\) and one on \(H_3(B\Gamma_H;\mathbb Z)\), yielding decompositions \(\pi_1(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty)\cong \mathbb R\oplus \ker(GV)\) and \(H_3(B\Gamma_H;\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb R\oplus \ker(GV)\). Are the two kernels \(\ker(GV:\pi_1(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty)\to\mathbb R)\) and \(\ker(GV:H_3(B\Gamma_H;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb R)\) trivial? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, because the paper explicitly records the splittings above, is the Godbillon-Vey map an isomorphism in each case; that is, do we have \(\pi_1(B\bar\Gamma_1^\infty)\cong \mathbb R\) and \(H_3(B\Gamma_H;\mathbb Z)\cong \mathbb R\) via \(GV\)? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
justification: This is clearly the intended target because your draft is almost verbatim the statement of Question 9.11 in §9.3.1. The immediately preceding paragraph is exactly where the paper defines the hidden notation behind “these two kerGV’s”: it introduces \(\Gamma_H\) via \(B\bar\Gamma_1^\omega\simeq K(\Gamma_H,1)\), states the surjective Godbillon-Vey map to \(\mathbb R\), and records the two split decompositions whose kernels are being asked about. A faithful rewrite therefore has to unpack those two kernels and no more; broadening to nearby Questions 9.12–9.14 would change the problem. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

citations.label: paragraph immediately preceding Question 9.11 (definition of \(\Gamma_H\), the GV surjections, and the two split decompositions)
